name: Lentiviral vector (HIV-1-derived)
short_description: HIV-1 rebuilt as a gene-delivery shuttle — almost the entire viral genome removed, the packaging genes split across separate producer-cell plasmids, leaving a VSV-G-pseudotyped envelope and the conical Gag capsid to deliver a therapeutic cargo gene (flanked by self-inactivating LTRs) that reverse transcriptase and integrase write into the target cell's genome. Replication-incompetent: it cannot make more of itself.

sem.1: PASS - measured: dense, evenly-spaced round studs cover the whole visible surface (denser than the hiv key's sparse ~10-14-knob SEM), cool teal-blue false colour (deliberately distinct from hiv's amber/bronze), shallow depth of field, dark uncluttered substrate; correctly shows NO internal structure (SEM = surface only); no baked text/scale bar; edge-pixel scan confirms fill to all four edges (bg ~46-49/50-53/53-57 RGB on every edge, no border stripe). No labels per house rule (sem gets none).

textbook.1: FAIL - measured on a zoomed crop: the capsid rendered as a flat-topped trapezoid/wedge (a straight horizontal top edge), not a cone — does NOT read as conical. Dense VSV-G spike coat and single-strand RNA were correct, but the capsid shape was the disqualifying miss.
textbook.2: PASS - re-rendered with explicit dome/bullet-taper language; zoomed crop confirms the capsid now tapers smoothly from a wide base to a rounded point, reading clearly as conical (the clearest conical read after 3d). Single RNA strand confirmed via zoomed crop (one line, 4 separate enzyme dots, no second parallel strand). Dense, uniform VSV-G spike coat distinct from hiv's sparse pattern. Muted educational palette, thin outlines, no baked text. Edge-pixel scan confirms fill to all four edges (bg ~51-53/55-57/60-61 RGB, no border). Chosen as label base.

3d.1: PASS - measured on a zoomed crop: capsid is a clean tapered bullet/cone with a rounded point — the best conical read of the four accepted styles. Zoomed crop of the RNA confirms a single continuous purple strand (no second strand, not a double helix). Spike coat is moderately dense (roughly 30-40 visible spikes on the visible hemisphere) — visibly denser than hiv's sparse ~10-14 but not as uniformly dense as the sem/textbook/watercolor renders of this same subject; flagged as a minor cross-style inconsistency rather than re-rolled, since the primary do-NOT-draw risks (icosahedral capsid, double helix, sparse-only spikes) were all avoided. Natural biological tones, no baked text. Edge-pixel scan confirms fill to all four edges (bg ~1-2/6-7/16-17 RGB, dark navy, no border).

watercolor.1: FAIL - measured on a zoomed crop: the capsid cone shape was acceptable, but the RNA cargo was painted as TWO intertwined strands in different colours (dusty pink + blue-grey) — reads as a double helix, a direct do-NOT-draw violation. First fix attempt (recolouring to a single hue with a gradient) did not address the underlying two-strand structure.
watercolor.2: FAIL - capsid shape improved to a clean tapering cone/dome, but the zoomed crop still showed two distinct intertwined strands (pink + teal) inside the capsid — same double-helix violation, fix prompt insufficiently forceful.
watercolor.3: PASS - rewrote the fix prompt to explicitly forbid a second line/colour and describe enzymes as dots only; zoomed crop confirms exactly ONE continuous dusty-rose thread with 4 separate small green dots (no second strand of any colour). Capsid reads clearly as a tapering cone with a rounded point. Dense, uniform VSV-G spike coat. Aged paper fills the frame edge-to-edge — edge-pixel scan confirms warm paper tan on all four edges (~224-230/182-198/120-147 RGB), no white margin, no frame, no mat.

reference: PASS - CDC PHIL #10860 (public domain, CDC/Dr. A. Harrison, Dr. P. Feorino, 1989): colorized TEM of 2-3 clearly resolved, isolated mature HIV-1 virions (magenta envelope, dense dark core) against a uniform green background; normalised 1080x1080 crop has no baked-in text, caption, scale bar or border. This is an HIV-1 plate, NOT a lentiviral-vector-specific image — no freely-licensed vector-specific micrograph could be found (Wikimedia Commons, CDC PHIL, NIAID/NIH Flickr and general web search all checked; the one vector-specific TEM figure found, in Molecular Therapy, is CC BY-NC-ND and was excluded on licence grounds). Disclosed explicitly in the caption per the chlamydia-felis precedent. Free/mature (non-budding) particles were chosen deliberately over a budding-from-cell scene as the more honest visual analogue for a purified, manufactured vector product.
decision: attempt 1 capsid read as a flat-topped wedge, not conical (measured) — re-rendered; attempt 2 conical capsid confirmed by zoomed crop, single RNA strand confirmed, dense VSV-G spike coat, edge-to-edge fill measured
dense uniform false-colour stud coat, cool teal palette distinct from hiv's amber SEM, surface-only (correct for SEM), edge-to-edge fill measured, no labels per house rule

clearest conical capsid read of the set (zoomed crop), single RNA strand confirmed, spike density denser than hiv but less dense than this subject's other 3 styles (flagged, not re-rolled), edge-to-edge fill measured

attempts 1-2 painted the RNA as two intertwined strands (double-helix violation, measured on zoomed crop) despite a conical capsid; attempt 3 fixed to a single confirmed strand, conical capsid, dense spike coat, aged paper fills frame edge-to-edge (measured)
verified as-is (disclosed as HIV-1, not vector-specific)
